newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse at record closing high.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse at record closing high.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares ended bourse dealings above the magical 2,800 point level for the first time ever on Tuesday, spurred on by another record on Wall Street overnight and a firmer dollar.
The DAX index ended up 11.45 points, or 0.41 percent, at 2,810.64 points, earlier touching a bourse record high of 2,819.95 points, before slipping back slightly on profit-taking.
The IBIS DAX index, tracking day-long computer trade in the DAX index, earlier made an all-time high of 2,821.95 points.
"Everyone just keeps buying. We're seeing a cross-the-board rally," said one trader.

Dealers said the stronger dollar, which pulled above the 1.52 mark level late on Monday and continued to climb on Tuesday, was helping the chemical and auto sectors in particular, both of which are export-oriented and benefit from a weaker mark.
In the car sector, BMW and Daimler-Benz AG stocks were both charging ahead. BMW shares gained 32 marks, over three percent, to 985 marks, and Daimler rose 78 pfennigs to 99.88 marks.
Daimler broke through the 100 mark level in computer dealings, but could not repeat the performance in floor trade.
Amongst the chemical companies, BASF AG, Hoechst AG and Bayer AG were all stronger than the market trend.
Meanwhile, shares in troubled construction firm Philip Holzmann took a tumble, falling 18.50 marks, or almost five percent, to 367.50 marks.
Traders said the stock was reacting to a hike in the loss forecast for the company published by the research arm of Deutsche Bank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Dealers said they saw the current rally continuing until at least the end of the year, with 2,850 points the next major technical resistance level for the DAX to test.
But they said volumes could trail off at the end of the week, with the Thanksgiving public holiday in the U.S on Thursday.
